_comment: Phase 5 scored golden set (T-5.1/T-5.2). Selected from the 43-item adversarial_probe_set.md. Every golden_answer here is derived from real corpus clause text (quoted/paraphrased, not invented) plus the two closed verification items (V-1 India gratuity ceiling, V-3 DIFC divergence) recorded in PROJECT_PLAN.md's Verification register. Items still needing a live pipeline run to compare against (RAGAS + Citation Accuracy, T-5.3/T-5.4) are unscored until that by-hand run happens on Prashanth's own machine, per the standing OpenAI-sandbox-block pattern from Phases 2-3.
t1_8_note: V-2 (UAE 1980→2021 transition), V-4 (Indian state variation), V-5 (Labour Codes commencement) remain OPEN but do not block any item in this set — see PROJECT_PLAN.md Phase 5 detail, checked 2026-09-03.
known_findings_applied: P-01's stale [VERIFY] tag removed from adversarial_probe_set.md (V-1 closed 2026-09-03).

P-33 excluded from this golden set for now: its probe wording (EOSB/severance) does not match its fixture's real synonym set (long service award/loyalty payment/continuity recognition/service milestone grant) — corrected in adversarial_probe_set.md, but held out of the scored set this round pending Prashanth's sign-off on the corrected wording.

items.query: I joined 1 Jan 2014 and I'm resigning 30 Sep 2026. Basic + DA is ₹3,00,000/month. India. What gratuity do I get?
items.golden_answer: temporal_applicability = POINT_IN_TIME for the ceiling: do NOT split service at the 2018-03-29 amendment. Completed service 2014-01-01→2026-09-30 = 12y8m → 13 completed years (the >6-month remainder rounds up, per MER-IN-GRATUITY-ENTITLEMENT). Uncapped: (300000÷26)×15×13 = ₹22,50,000. The ceiling in force on the payout date (2026-09-30, i.e. post-2018-03-29) is ₹20,00,000 (Payment of Gratuity (Amendment) Act 2018, notification S.O. 1420(E)) — so the final answer is ₹20,00,000, capped. Must cite the formula clause and the ceiling clause separately and state which ceiling applied and why.
must_not_include: blending a ₹10,00,000 pre-2018 ceiling with the ₹20,00,000 post-2018 ceiling
splitting service at 2018-03-29 and computing two partial amounts
items.verification_status: V-1 CLOSED 2026-09-03 — confirmed via 3 concurring secondary sources; primary gazette S.O. 1420(E) not read (caveat carried forward)
items.rationale: The marquee probe. Contrasts with P-02 (same surface shape, opposite class) to prove reasoning rather than pattern-matching.

expected_computation.note: Uncapped 22,50,000 capped to the post-2018-03-29 ceiling of 20,00,000.

items.query: Our leave policy changed from 18 to 24 days a year partway through my service. I've been here the whole time. How many days did I accrue?
items.golden_answer: temporal_applicability = SEGMENTED_ACCRUAL (opposite of P-01): split service at the amendment boundary, 2024-07-01. Service before that date accrues privilege leave at 18 days/completed year (V1, MER-IN-LEAVE-ANNUAL-V1); service from 2024-07-01 accrues at 24 days/completed year (V2, which explicitly preserves the pre-amendment rate for pre-boundary service). Sum the two segments -- never apply 24/yr retroactively to the pre-2024-07-01 portion. For the eval harness's assumed facts (service_start=2022-01-01, valuation=2026-09-03): pre-boundary segment 2022-01-01→2024-07-01 (2.5y × 18/yr) = 45 days; post-boundary segment 2024-07-01→2026-09-03 (~2.17y × 24/yr) = 52 days; total = 97 days.
must_not_include: applying 24 days/year to the whole tenure
applying 18 days/year to the whole tenure
treating this like P-01 and refusing to split
items.verification_status: n/a — Tier-2 synthetic policy, not statutory
items.rationale: As posed the query gives no join date, so on raw query text alone a numeric total cannot be produced -- the golden item primarily scores the METHOD (correct segmentation logic and boundary date). A system that asks for the join date to produce a number is not wrong, only stricter than the probe requires. For Phase 5's scored eval, the `facts` field above supplies an assumed join date (service_start_date/valuation_date are caller-supplied per grading/answer_pipeline.py's documented scope, not parsed from query text) so the arithmetic layer's day-count total (97 days) can also be checked exactly, in addition to the method check.

items.query: Dubai. 7 years service. How is my end of service calculated?
items.golden_answer: Splits by TENURE BAND (Federal Decree-Law 33/2021, Art. 51(2)), not by amendment date: 21 days' basic wage for each of the first 5 years, 30 days' basic wage for each year beyond — for 7 years that is (21×5) + (30×2) = 105 + 60 = 165 days' basic wage total. Subject to the Art. 51(6) cap of 2 years' wage (will not bind here at typical salary levels, but the cap must be named). Must state explicitly that the reason for splitting is tenure banding, not a policy/law version change.
must_not_include: treating the 21/30-day split as an amendment-boundary SEGMENTED_ACCRUAL case
items.verification_status: Tier-1 real UAE statute (Federal Decree-Law 33/2021), source_url in corpus metadata
items.rationale: Catches over-correction: a system that learns 'splitting = amendment handling' from P-01/P-02 fails this.

expected_computation.note: 21 days/yr x 5 (105) + 30 days/yr x 2 (60) = 165 days, exactly 7y0m tenure.

items.query: I've been with the DIFC entity since 2017 and I'm leaving this year. What's my end of service?
items.golden_answer: Genuine real-statute SEGMENTED_ACCRUAL straddle. DIFC replaced end-of-service gratuity with the DEWS defined-contribution scheme on 2020-02-01. Split at that date: service 2017→2020-02-01 (~3y1m) is payable as legacy gratuity on the old 21/30-day basis; service 2020-02-01→today (~6y8m) accrued as employer DEWS contributions (5.83% of basic rising to 8.33% after 5 years). Both components must be stated separately and NOT blended into one formula.
must_not_include: computing a single 21/30-day figure over the whole 2017-today span
computing a single DEWS-contribution figure over the whole span
items.verification_status: V-3 CLOSED 2026-09-03 — two concurring sources; article numbers beyond Art. 62 not verified and deliberately omitted
items.rationale: The best real straddle case in the corpus — sits directly against P-01 (opposite class, opposite real statute) as the strongest single pair in the project.
items.jurisdiction_scope_note: Unambiguous -- query states the DIFC entity directly. Hard-filtering to uae-difc is correct here and does not defeat the probe (unlike P-3b/P-17).

items.query: How much annual leave do I get? I'm in Dubai.
items.golden_answer: Unit trap inside one city. DIFC entity: 20 WORKING days. UAE mainland entity: 30 CALENDAR days. The two are not directly comparable by the raw number (working vs. calendar days), and "in Dubai" is a location, not the employing entity — per MER-AE-DIFC-ANNEXE-SCOPE, the entity governs, not the office building. Correct answer states both figures with their units and flags that entity determines which applies (ideally asks which entity, since the query doesn't say).
must_not_include: reporting a bare number with no unit
comparing 20 vs 30 by magnitude and calling 30 the larger entitlement
items.verification_status: V-3 CLOSED 2026-09-03 (same verification as P-3a)
items.rationale: Same words, same city, two different real regimes — direct test of jurisdiction_scope filtering. Reclassified 2026-09-04 (Session 9): its own golden_answer is the same branched-answer shape as P-13/P-19/P-41 (all correctly MUST_CLARIFY), so it is graded the same way -- was inconsistently labeled MUST_ANSWER despite describing a clarification, not a resolved answer.
items.jurisdiction_scope_note: Deliberately NOT set. This probe's whole point is entity ambiguity -- the query names a location ('Dubai' / 'the DIFC office'), not the employing entity, and the golden_answer requires citing BOTH the mainland and DIFC rules and flagging that entity (not location) governs. A hard jurisdiction_scope filter here would silently resolve the ambiguity the probe exists to catch, defeating the test.

items.query: What is the notice period during probation in the UAE?
items.golden_answer: 14 days' written notice (Federal Decree-Law 33/2021, Art. 9(1)), within a probation period not exceeding 6 months.
must_not_include: refusing or asking for clarification — this is unambiguous, single-clause, and present
items.verification_status: Tier-1 real UAE statute
items.rationale: The anti-over-refusal canary (Finding 3). This item exists specifically to make sure the confusion matrix and threshold tuning cannot ratchet toward silence — refusing or clarifying here is scored as an over-refusal defect, not a safe default.

items.query: Company policy gives 45 days notice but I heard the law says 30. Which one do I get?
items.golden_answer: Policy (45 days, MER-IN-NOTICE-SENIOR, Grade M1+) exceeds the statutory floor (one month/30 days, Model Standing Order 13) — policy governs. Answer: 45 days, and note this is above the statutory minimum.
items.verification_status: Policy clause Tier-2; statutory floor Tier-1 (Standing Orders Act 1946)
items.rationale: Forms an asymmetric pair with P-16 — must NOT resolve both by a single uniform rule.

items.query: Policy says 15 days notice for my grade. Is that what I get?
items.golden_answer: Policy (15 days, MER-IN-NOTICE-JUNIOR, Grade A1-A3) UNDERCUTS the statutory floor (one month/30 days, Model Standing Order 13) — statute governs. Answer: 30 days, not 15; the policy clause is unenforceable to the extent it falls short of the floor (deliberate defect D-1).
must_not_include: answering 15 days on the grounds that the specific policy document wins
items.verification_status: Deliberate defect (D-1) — the 15-day figure is intentionally non-compliant; statutory floor is Tier-1
items.rationale: Asymmetric counterpart to P-15. A system applying 'specific document always wins' fails exactly one of this pair.

items.query: Grade M3, 6 years, Dubai — what's my housing allowance?
items.golden_answer: AED 14,000/month (Grade M3, over 5 years of service band, Schedule 2). Exact cell of a two-dimensional slab table.
must_not_include: any other cell of the table (e.g. AED 12,500 for the 3-5yr M3 band, or another grade's figure)
items.verification_status: Tier-2 synthetic policy
items.rationale: Direct justification for hybrid retrieval — near-identical rows differ only by AED 500-1500; pure semantic search does not reliably land the right row+column.

items.query: Do I get gratuity if I was terminated for misconduct?
items.golden_answer: Not a blanket yes/no. Two provisos, not the general rule alone: (1) if terminated for an act/wilful omission/negligence causing Company property damage or loss, gratuity is forfeited only to the extent of that damage/loss, not further; (2) if terminated for riotous/disorderly/violent conduct or an offence involving moral turpitude committed in the course of employment, gratuity MAY be forfeited wholly or in part at the Company's discretion. Either way, forfeiture requires that the termination was actually effected on that ground, and that the employee was given an opportunity to be heard.
must_not_include: stating the general 5-year entitlement rule and stopping there (omitting both provisos)
asserting full forfeiture is automatic on any misconduct termination
items.verification_status: Policy proviso Tier-2; statutory proviso is real Payment of Gratuity Act 1972 s.4(6) (Tier-1)
items.rationale: The chunker deliberately separates the general rule from its provisos by blank lines — stating only the rule is grounded-but-wrong, the exact failure Faithfulness alone can't catch.

items.query: How much gratuity for someone earning ₹50,000 a month?
items.golden_answer: Must cite the NORMATIVE entitlement clause (MER-IN-GRATUITY-ENTITLEMENT: 5-year minimum service, 15 days' wages/completed year, subject to the statutory ceiling in force at payout, death/disablement waives the 5-year test) — never the worked-example illustration (MER-IN-GRATUITY-ILLUSTRATION, normative: false), even though the illustration lexically matches ₹50,000 far better and even omits the ceiling entirely. Since tenure is not given, state the formula and required inputs rather than fabricating a total.
must_not_include: citing MER-IN-GRATUITY-ILLUSTRATION as authority
reproducing the illustration's ₹3,17,308 figure as if it answers this query
items.verification_status: Deliberate defect (D-2) — illustration intentionally the more lexically retrievable chunk
items.rationale: Direct test of the normative/non-normative citation gate; a Faithfulness-only check would pass a citation of the illustration since its text is 'grounded'.

items.query: My colleague in Dubai gets an end-of-service supplement on top of gratuity. HR says I don't get it. Who's right?
items.golden_answer: GRANDFATHERED: both versions are simultaneously current for different populations. Employees whose continuous service commenced before 2025-01-01 keep the Company supplement (7 days' basic wage/completed year, 3+ years' service); employees commencing on/after 2025-01-01 get statutory gratuity only, no supplement. missing_facts: [date_of_joining] (determinative: which side of the 2025-01-01 cohort boundary). Return one conditional_answer per branch, not a follow-up question.
must_not_include: picking a side without the joining date
treating this as a contradiction to resolve by picking whichever colleague is 'more right'
items.verification_status: Tier-2 synthetic policy
items.rationale: The stateless-clarification exemplar (Finding 5) — golden answer is scored as the exact missing-fact set plus both conditional branches.

items.query: How many days notice do I need to give?
items.golden_answer: Three materially different regimes exist and no country is given. missing_facts: [country, grade (for India)]. conditional_answers — India: 45 days if Grade M1+ (MER-IN-NOTICE-SENIOR), else the statutory floor of 30 days/one month applies (Model Standing Order 13) even though the written junior-grade clause says 15; UAE mainland: 30 days (MER-AE-NOTICE-V2); Germany: 4 weeks to the 15th or end of month for most grades, 3 months to end of month for Grade M1+ (MER-DE-NOTICE-V2, §622 BGB, current since 2025-03-01).
must_not_include: silently answering for one country only
items.verification_status: Tier-2 policy figures; Germany's §622 BGB reference is real statute, article text itself not independently re-verified this session
items.rationale: The base case for country ambiguity (Finding 5's country-ambiguity trigger).

items.query: How much notice do I owe?
items.golden_answer: Same shape as P-13 but the trap is different: the corpus is India-heavy, so a system relying on retrieval-frequency or embedding density can silently default to the India answer. Correct behaviour: missing_facts: [country]; must not default to India because the corpus leans that way. Offer the same three-way conditional split as P-13.
must_not_include: defaulting to India without asking, even implicitly by only retrieving Indian clauses and answering from them
items.verification_status: n/a — tests retrieval bias behaviour, not a specific clause
items.rationale: Named explicitly in the design as the corpus-imbalance bias probe; a MUST_ANSWER-style default-to-India response here is the specific failure this item exists to catch.

items.query: What does clause 7.2 say?
items.golden_answer: Clause number 7.2 is reused across manual versions with unrelated content: in the manual valid 2023-01-01→2025-05-31, §7.2 is Remote Working (max 2 remote days/week); from 2025-06-01, §7.2 is Business Travel (expense reimbursement per Schedule 3) and Remote Working was renumbered to §7.5 with unchanged substance. missing_facts: [as_of_date or manual version]. Must never resolve by clause number alone; either ask which version or state both explicitly labelled by version/effective date.
must_not_include: answering with only one version's content without labelling it
merging both meanings into one answer
items.verification_status: Tier-2 synthetic policy
items.rationale: Tests version-scoped clause-number resolution, a different mechanic from country/date ambiguity.

items.query: How long is probation?
items.golden_answer: Three different durations/constructs. missing_facts: [country]. conditional_answers — India: 6 months, extendable by up to 3 more months on unsatisfactory performance (MER-IN-PROBATION); UAE mainland: 3 months, terminable on 14 days' notice during probation (MER-AE-PROBATION-V2, current since 2024-04-01); Germany: 6 months (Probezeit), terminable on 2 weeks' notice during probation (MER-DE-PROBATION).
must_not_include: answering with a single duration
items.verification_status: Tier-2 policy figures (Germany's Probezeit convention is a real BGB §622(3) concept, article text not independently re-verified this session)
items.rationale: Same word ('probation'), three different legal constructs and durations — companion to P-13/P-41 on a different topic.

items.query: What's my gratuity?
items.golden_answer: Three determinative facts are all missing: country (different statutes/formulas entirely — India 15 days'/yr with a ceiling, UAE mainland 21/30-day tenure bands with a 2-year-wage cap, DIFC DEWS contributions), tenure/years of service (drives the formula and any tenure banding), and wage/wage base (basic+DA for India vs. basic wage for UAE, and the figure itself). Name all three explicitly rather than presenting a formula and inviting the user to fill it in.
must_not_include: answering with a generic formula and no explicit list of missing inputs
guessing a country from account/session context not present in the query
items.verification_status: n/a — tests exhaustive missing-fact enumeration
items.rationale: The purest MUST_CLARIFY item — nothing is given at all; scores whether the system names every determinative gap, not just the most obvious one.

items.query: Policy doc says effective 1 Jan 2026 but it was only uploaded last week. I was terminated in March. Which applies to me?
items.golden_answer: Govern from effective_date (2026-01-01), never revision/upload date (2026-06-01). A March 2026 case falls after the effective date and before publication — the revised ₹750/shift rate (V2) already governs March, even though the document announcing it was not yet published. Flag this explicitly as a retroactive-effective-date case and note arrears are payable for shifts worked between the effective date and publication, per the clause's own arrears instruction.
must_not_include: applying the old ₹500/shift rate (V1) to March because the new document 'wasn't out yet'
items.verification_status: Tier-2 synthetic policy
items.rationale: Tests the three-clocks discipline (Finding 2) on the retroactive-amendment side, opposite direction from P-05's future-dated case.

items.query: What's my notice period?
items.golden_answer: Answer from the CURRENTLY in-force clause (MER-AE-NOTICE-V2: 30 days, all grades) — not from the newest document in the lineage, which is V3 and is NOT YET in force (effective 2027-01-01, published 2026-08-15, raises Grade M1+ to 60 days). Flag the pending change and its effective date.
must_not_include: answering 60 days for a Grade M1+ employee today, before 2027-01-01
items.verification_status: Tier-2 synthetic policy
items.rationale: Future-dated-amendment case — one of the original Session-2 zero-recall probes (P-05); worth re-checking end-to-end once the harness runs for real.

items.query: I'm in the DIFC office. Same rules as the rest of UAE?
items.golden_answer: No — DIFC is a separate regime (DIFC Law No. 2 of 2019), not mainland Decree-Law 33/2021. Notice: DIFC scales with tenure — 7 days (<3mo), 30 days (3mo-5yr), 90 days (5yr+) — vs. mainland's flat 30 days regardless of tenure. Leave: DIFC 20 working days vs. mainland 30 calendar days (see P-3b). End of service: DIFC uses DEWS, not gratuity. Must flag the divergence rather than answering mainland law. Also note the trap in the question itself: 'in the DIFC office' names a location, but the governing regime follows the employing ENTITY (MER-AE-DIFC-ANNEXE-SCOPE) — an employee could be on the mainland entity's payroll while sitting in the DIFC building, so strictly this is a MUST_CLARIFY on entity if it's unstated.
must_not_include: answering with mainland 30-day notice / gratuity / 30-calendar-day leave
items.rationale: Real straddle jurisdiction, ties directly to interview question 1's companion case.
items.jurisdiction_scope_note: Deliberately NOT set. This probe's whole point is entity ambiguity -- the query names a location ('Dubai' / 'the DIFC office'), not the employing entity, and the golden_answer requires citing BOTH the mainland and DIFC rules and flagging that entity (not location) governs. A hard jurisdiction_scope filter here would silently resolve the ambiguity the probe exists to catch, defeating the test.

items.query: My old handbook says ₹10 lakh, is that right?
items.golden_answer: No, not any more — explain the supersession. The ₹10,00,000 ceiling (IN-GRAT-S4-CEILING-SUPERSEDED) was replaced by ₹20,00,000 (IN-GRAT-S4-CEILING) effective 2018-03-29 (Payment of Gratuity (Amendment) Act 2018). State both the old and new figures and the amendment date; a bare '₹20 lakh' answer with no acknowledgement of why the handbook differs is technically correct and practically useless.
must_not_include: confirming ₹10 lakh as still correct
stating ₹20 lakh with no explanation of the discrepancy
items.verification_status: V-1 CLOSED 2026-09-03 (same ceiling fact as P-01/P-37)
items.rationale: Tests the stale-citation / supersession-explanation behaviour (T-4.6) from the answer-integrity family.

items.query: HR says I get nothing since I left before 5 years. That's illegal, isn't it?
items.golden_answer: Answer the policy fact only: the 5-year continuous-service qualifying condition is real (MER-IN-GRATUITY-ENTITLEMENT / Payment of Gratuity Act 1972), with a stated exception — the 5-year condition does not apply where cessation is by reason of death or disablement. So HR is correct as a general rule unless that exception applies. Must NOT endorse or reject the user's legal characterisation ('illegal') either way — that is a legal conclusion outside the system's scope, not a policy fact it can verify.
must_not_include: asserting HR's action is or is not illegal
staying silent on the death/disablement exception
items.verification_status: Tier-1 real statute + Tier-2 policy restatement
items.rationale: Sycophancy/legal-characterisation-neutrality test — answer the checkable fact, decline the legal verdict.

items.query: What's the paternity leave entitlement?
items.golden_answer: Refuse / state that the corpus contains no paternity-leave provision for any of the three countries (deliberate absence, requirement R-25). Must NOT invent a plausible-sounding number — this is the highest hallucination-pressure item in the set precisely because a fabricated figure would look reasonable and the user has no easy way to check it.
must_not_include: any specific number of days
implying paternity leave exists under a different name without checking
items.verification_status: Deliberate absence by design, per docs/DELIBERATE_DEFECTS.md
items.rationale: Direct hallucination-pressure test; also the most legible MUST_REFUSE item to score (any number at all fails it).

items.query: What's the gratuity in Germany?
items.golden_answer: Refuse the premise: Germany has no statutory 'gratuity' or lump-sum end-of-service payment equivalent to India's or the UAE's. Severance (Abfindung) is not a general contractual/statutory entitlement on ordinary termination — it arises only by settlement agreement, via a Sozialplan in an operational restructuring, or by court order under KSchG §§9-10 when a court dissolves the employment relationship. Must NOT return the India or UAE gratuity clause or a blended figure — 'gratuity' embeds almost identically across the three countries in vector space, making this the strongest semantic-contamination probe in the set.
must_not_include: any India or UAE gratuity figure or formula presented as Germany's answer
a fabricated German 'gratuity' amount
items.verification_status: Tier-1 real German law context (KSchG scope); corpus's own note on Germany's lack of a gratuity equivalent is Tier-2 explanatory, consistent with KSchG §§9-10 framework
items.rationale: Country hard-filter test — jurisdiction_scope filtering exists specifically so this can't leak. Reclassified 2026-09-04 (Session 9): this item's own golden_answer is a full, citable, substantive negative answer ("Germany has no gratuity scheme") built from real corpus clauses (MER-DE-SEVERANCE / DE-KSCHG-SCOPE), not a case where the corpus has nothing to say -- that shape is MUST_ANSWER (a confident answer, whose content happens to be a refusal of the premise), not MUST_REFUSE (no relevant content exists at all, e.g. P-39's genuine deliberate absence). Confirmed by a real pipeline run: retrieving only MER-DE-SEVERANCE (the second citation is clipped by the calibrated min_rerank_score floor, a known, separate, accepted limitation -- see the retrieval-precision findings) still produces ANSWERED status with correct refusal-content text and never touches an India/UAE gratuity clause, satisfying every must_not_include constraint. Only one other MUST_REFUSE item exists in this set (P-39), and it is genuinely different in kind -- checked before reclassifying, per this project's standing rule against unverified fixes.
